quiz.q: According to Fareed Zakaria, why has democracy struggled to succeed in many post-colonial Third World nations?
options: Economic development was prioritized over establishing formal democratic procedures and regular elections.
Cultural traditions in these societies completely rejected Western concepts of human dignity and individual rights.
Constitutionalism and the rule of law were not established before introducing universal adult franchise.
Global institutions failed to provide adequate economic assistance to newly independent developing nations.
quiz.why: Zakaria argues that constitutionalism and the rule of law must precede democracy, and its absence explains democratic failures in Third World countries.

quiz.q: How does Amartya Sen counter the "Lee Thesis" regarding the relationship between democracy and development?
options: He argues democracy is an essential precondition that expands human capabilities through health and education.
He claims economic growth automatically guarantees human freedom without needing state investment in social sectors.
He asserts that authoritarian governance is initially required before citizens become fit for democratic rights.
He proves that rapid industrial growth must precede any political democratization in developing societies.
quiz.why: Sen argues that democracy is a precondition for development because public investment in education and health builds essential human capabilities.

quiz.q: Why does Robert Dahl characterize modern liberal democracies as "polyarchies" rather than ideal democracies or oligarchies?
options: They concentrate supreme political authority within a single monolithic elite that strictly forbids dissent.
They enable direct citizen decision-making on all state legislation without relying on elected representatives.
They eliminate all social conflicts by guaranteeing complete economic equality among competing interest groups.
They operate through open interest-group competition that realistically approximates democratic ideals in practice.
quiz.why: Dahl explains polyarchy as an "approximate democracy" where politics functions through competing interest groups rather than pure mass rule or closed oligarchy.

quiz.q: According to C.B. Macpherson, what transformation is required for Western liberal democracies to become genuinely egalitarian?
options: Restricting developmental power exclusively to the state while preserving capitalist ownership of resources.
Eliminating coercive extractive power entirely while ensuring equal developmental creative power for all citizens.
Replacing competitive elections with an unelected administrative bureaucracy to manage social welfare distribution.
Maximizing the extractive power of workers to forcibly counterbalance the economic dominance of capitalists.
quiz.why: Macpherson argues that true egalitarian democracy requires eliminating coercive extractive power while providing equal developmental power, defined as creative freedom, to everyone.
